description:
FILED s449/s450 (Fable, round-8 review of agent U) from an own probe.  PRE-EXISTING -- identical on pre-#477 main (eager $&) and after (lazy offsets); nothing to do with U-s change, which only made the reviewer look.

REPRO (perl 5.40.3):
    "zq" =~ /(z)/;
    $_ = "p1 p2 p3";
    while (/(p\d)/g) { }          # three successful matches inside
    print "one=[$1] amp=[$&]\n";
        perl: one=[z] amp=[z]     -- the PRE-loop match is RESTORED at block exit
        PCL:  one=[p3] amp=[p3]   -- last successful match, kept globally

perlre: the match variables are "dynamically scoped until the end of the enclosing block or until the next successful match".  PCL implements the second half (a FAILED match keeps the previous values -- probed, correct) and specific frames (sort comparators), but not the general block-exit restore.  ir-spec SS8-s "dynamically saved/restored around scopes like Perl" overstates what is implemented -- fix the doc or the runtime together.

COST OF FIXING: a save/restore of the whole match state around EVERY block is a hot-path price (the #477 lesson: offsets are cheap to save, memos/subject pointers too -- the state is now 6 slots + the capture group array, so a block save is O(groups), not O(subject)).  Measure which suite rows sit behind it before building; the while-//g-then-read idiom is the common spelling.

BAR: the repro + the failed-match inverse + a sort-comparator frame check vs perl; the op/+re/ companion legs (cl/ change); Target-A guard that the m//g loop timing curve stays linear.
subject: Match variables are BLOCK-scoped in perl -- leaving the enclosing block RESTORES $&/$1/../%+ to the pre-block match; PCL keeps last-successful globally (visible after every while-//g loop)
